#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-1] A run hook that hangs is killed at the per-stage timeout on
# every dispatch route — map, fanout, sequential strategy, roleless leaf, cycle
# member, parallel-group member, and always_run — and the stage ends with
# disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run and _orch_local_collect_results
# kill through zbuild_pg_kill; no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for
# stage dispatch.
#
# All dispatch routes reach plugin_hook_call in lifecycle.sh; the single
# watchdog there covers every route. These tests FAIL on pre-change code
# (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog) and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-1/SPEC-10] per-dispatch stage timeout watchdog"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-dispatch"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"

# ─── Extract plugin_hook_call body for inspection ────────────────────────────
_phc_body=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] lifecycle.sh has a per-dispatch timeout watchdog ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call has a timeout watchdog for the run hook"

if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh"

    # The watchdog must be armed only for the `run` hook (not cleanup/other hooks).
    # Check for a guard like `[[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]` near the timeout code.
    if grep -qE '"run"' <<< "$_phc_body" && grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' <<< "$_phc_body"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog in plugin_hook_call is guarded to run hook only" \
            "zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill not found inside plugin_hook_call — no per-dispatch watchdog"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] the watchdog writes timed_out disposition ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] watchdog writes disposition timed_out"

# The watchdog must call the disposition layer with 'timed_out' when it fires.
# Check lifecycle.sh and disposition-writing helpers used from within lifecycle.sh.
_timed_out_found=0
if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null; then
    _timed_out_found=1
fi
# Also check that the runner or a helper wires the watchdog result to timed_out
_runner="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
if grep -q 'timed_out' "$_runner" 2>/dev/null; then
    _timed_out_found=1
fi

if [[ "$_timed_out_found" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out disposition is used in the dispatch path" \
        "'timed_out' not found in lifecycle.sh or runner.sh — timeout result cannot produce the required disposition"
fi

# After the change: the timed_out event must name the stage and the limit.
# The requirement says "ends with disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit".
# Check that the emit_event call for plugin.run.timed_out in lifecycle.sh carries
# both stage= and timeout_s= fields.
_timed_out_event_ctx=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _timed_out_event_ctx="$(grep -A4 'plugin\.run\.timed_out' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)"
fi
if grep -q 'stage=' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx" && grep -q 'timeout_s=' <<< "$_timed_out_event_ctx"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out event names the stage (stage=) and the limit (timeout_s=)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] timed_out event names the stage (stage=) and the limit (timeout_s=)" \
        "plugin.run.timed_out event in lifecycle.sh is missing stage= or timeout_s= field"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] every dispatch route reaches plugin_hook_call ─────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] all dispatch routes lead through plugin_hook_call"

# The design states: all dispatch routes — map, fanout, sequential strategy,
# roleless leaf, cycle member, parallel-group member, always_run — reach
# plugin_hook_call. Verify that each strategy file and the runner itself calls
# plugin_hook_call (not a private bypass).
for _sf in \
    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh \
    core/pipeline/runner.sh; do
    _file="$REPO_ROOT/$_sf"
    [[ -f "$_file" ]] || continue
    if grep -q 'plugin_hook_call' "$_file"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] $_sf reaches plugin_hook_call (route covered by watchdog)" \
            "plugin_hook_call not found — this dispatch route would bypass the watchdog"
    fi
done

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] no hand-rolled TERM/KILL in lifecycle.sh for dispatch ────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] lifecycle.sh has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"

if [[ -n "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    # After the change: no `kill -TERM` or `kill -KILL` hand-rolled in
    # plugin_hook_call itself — these are replaced by zbuild_pg_kill.
    # Allow lines that are purely comments.
    _hand_rolled=""
    _hand_rolled="$(grep -E 'kill -TERM|kill -KILL' <<< "$_phc_body" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_hand_rolled" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
            "found: $(printf '%s' "$_hand_rolled" | head -3 | tr '\n' '|') — replace with zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] plugin_hook_call has no hand-rolled TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_collect_results uses zbuild_pg_kill"

_le="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/local_engine.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_le" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] core/orch/local_engine.sh exists" "not found"
else
    if grep -q 'zbuild_pg_kill\|zbuild_pid_kill' "$_le"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] local_engine.sh uses zbuild_pg_kill/zbuild_pid_kill" \
            "not found — _orch_local_collect_results still has a hand-rolled kill sequence"
    fi

    # The old _orch_local_kill_slot is replaced; if it still exists, that is a bug.
    if grep -q '_orch_local_kill_slot' "$_le"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh" \
            "still present — the hand-rolled kill helper was not replaced by zbuild_pg_kill"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _orch_local_kill_slot is removed from local_engine.sh"
    fi
fi

# ─── watchdog is backend-agnostic: lifecycle is above backends ────────────────
print_test_section "watchdog in lifecycle.sh is backend-agnostic (above the backend layer)"

# The watchdog's position in lifecycle.sh (plugin_hook_call) means it fires
# regardless of which orch backend is active — the backends dispatch work units
# that ultimately call plugin_hook_call. Verify orch-mock still routes through it.
_mock_plugin="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_mock_plugin" ]]; then
    assert_fail "plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # orch-mock dispatches work units that call plugin_hook_call;
    # the backend itself does not arm or disarm the watchdog.
    assert_pass "orch-mock plugin exists (backend-agnostic watchdog can be tested with it)"
fi

# ─── ruflo-hive carries no suppressing TERM/KILL sequence ─────────────────────
print_test_section "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh has no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"

_hive="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_hive" ]]; then
    assert_fail "plugins/tool/orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh exists" "not found"
else
    # The hive plugin must not have a kill -TERM / kill -KILL that would intercept
    # the lifecycle-level watchdog's signal before it reaches the hook subshell.
    # (Pool-management kills in the backend's own shutdown are acceptable.)
    _hive_kills=""
    _hive_kills="$(grep -n 'kill -TERM\|kill -KILL' "$_hive" | grep -v '^\s*#' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_hive_kills" ]]; then
        assert_fail "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch" \
            "found kill -TERM/-KILL in ruflo-hive — may suppress lifecycle-level watchdog signal:" \
            "$(printf '%s' "$_hive_kills" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
    else
        assert_pass "orch-ruflo-hive/plugin.sh carries no TERM/KILL for stage dispatch"
    fi
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-9] A configured orchestrator backend that cannot be found, or
# whose config is unreadable, fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the
# backend — tested from the installed tree.
#
# Before this change, orch_load_backend silently fell back to orch-sequential
# rather than failing with a clear error. After the change, a missing or
# unreadable backend causes the run to end as `misconfigured` with the backend
# name in the reason.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where a missing backend silently falls
# back instead of failing) and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-9] missing/unreadable orch backend → misconfigured"
setup_test_env "orch-backend-misconfigured"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-9] non-existent backend alias fails as misconfigured ─────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-9] orch_load_backend with unknown alias → misconfigured"

# Use a plugins root that has no backend with alias `no-such-backend`.
_out1=""
_rc1=0
_out1="$(
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
    bash -c '
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        orch_load_backend "no-such-backend" 2>&1
        echo "exit:$?"
    ' 2>&1)" || _rc1=$?

# After the change: the output or exit code signals misconfigured, and the
# backend name appears in the message.
if grep -qiE 'misconfigured|not found|cannot' <<< "$_out1" \
        && grep -q 'no-such-backend' <<< "$_out1"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-9] unknown backend alias produces misconfigured + names the backend"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-9] unknown backend alias produces misconfigured + names the backend" \
        "output did not name the backend or did not signal misconfigured:" \
        "$(printf '%s' "$_out1" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-9] the contract.sh fallback logic is gone ───────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-9] contract.sh has no fallback to orch-sequential"

_contract="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/contract.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_contract" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-9] core/orch/contract.sh exists" "file not found"
else
    # The old code: "Fallback: try built-in orch-sequential plugin by known path"
    # After the change this fallback is removed.
    if grep -q 'orch-sequential' "$_contract"; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-9] contract.sh has no fallback to orch-sequential" \
            "orch-sequential still referenced in contract.sh — the fallback was not removed"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-9] contract.sh has no fallback to orch-sequential"
    fi
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-9] orch_load_backend does not silently continue on missing ───
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-9] orch_load_backend fails (does not return 0) on missing backend"

_out2=""
_rc2=0
_out2="$(
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/empty-plugins" \
    bash -c '
        mkdir -p "'"$TEST_TEMP_DIR"'/empty-plugins"
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        orch_load_backend "missing-alias" 2>&1
        echo "exit:$?"
    ' 2>&1)" || _rc2=$?

# Extract the exit code the subshell reported
_reported_exit=""
_reported_exit="$(grep '^exit:' <<< "$_out2" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f2 || true)"

# After the change: orch_load_backend must not return 0 for a missing backend.
# (Old code: warns and returns 0, so the engine continued without a backend.)
if [[ "$_reported_exit" == "0" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-9] orch_load_backend returns non-zero on missing backend" \
        "returned 0 — a missing backend was silently accepted (pre-change fallback behaviour)"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-9] orch_load_backend returns non-zero on missing backend"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-9] unreadable backend config fails as misconfigured ─────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-9] unreadable backend manifest → misconfigured"

# Create a backend whose manifest.yaml is present but unreadable (chmod 000).
# contract.sh scans with find -type f, so the file is found; then grep for the
# orchestrator-backend role fails (permission denied, suppressed), the entry is
# skipped, and no backend is matched → misconfigured. This tests the
# "whose config is unreadable" arm of the SPEC-9 requirement.
_unreadable_plugins="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/unreadable-plugins"
mkdir -p "$_unreadable_plugins/tool/bad-backend"
cat > "$_unreadable_plugins/tool/bad-backend/manifest.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: bad-backend
name: Bad Backend
kind: tool
version: 0.0.1
roles:
  - orchestrator-backend
aliases:
  - alias: bad-backend
EOF
chmod 000 "$_unreadable_plugins/tool/bad-backend/manifest.yaml"

_out4=""
_out4="$(
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_unreadable_plugins" \
    bash -c '
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        orch_load_backend "bad-backend" 2>&1
        echo "exit:$?"
    ' 2>&1)" || true

# Restore so cleanup_test_env can remove it
chmod 644 "$_unreadable_plugins/tool/bad-backend/manifest.yaml" 2>/dev/null || true

_reported_exit4=""
_reported_exit4="$(grep '^exit:' <<< "$_out4" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f2 || true)"

# After the change: orch_load_backend must not return 0 for an unreadable config.
if [[ "$_reported_exit4" == "0" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-9] unreadable backend config fails as misconfigured (non-zero rc)" \
        "returned 0 — an unreadable backend config was silently accepted"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-9] unreadable backend config fails as misconfigured (non-zero rc)"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-19] installed-layout variant ────────────────────────────────
# SPEC-19: source contract.sh from a temp install directory produced by rsync
# (mirroring install.sh lines 74-80: scripts/ core/ plugins/ config/).
# The behavior must be identical from the installed layout.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-19] installed layout: sources contract.sh from tmp ZBUILD_HOME"

_zbuild_home="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/zbuild-home-install"
mkdir -p "$_zbuild_home"

if command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for _d in scripts core plugins config; do
        rsync -a "$REPO_ROOT/$_d/" "$_zbuild_home/$_d/" 2>/dev/null || true
    done

    # Unknown-alias case from the installed layout.
    _out_inst=""
    _out_inst="$(
        ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_zbuild_home/plugins" \
        bash -c '
            source "'"$_zbuild_home"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            source "'"$_zbuild_home"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            orch_load_backend "no-such-backend-installed" 2>&1
            echo "exit:$?"
        ' 2>&1)" || true

    # After the change: misconfigured output with the backend name.
    if grep -qiE 'misconfigured|not found|cannot' <<< "$_out_inst" \
            && grep -q 'no-such-backend-installed' <<< "$_out_inst"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-19] installed layout: unknown backend → misconfigured naming the backend"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-19] installed layout: unknown backend → misconfigured naming the backend" \
            "output: $(printf '%s' "$_out_inst" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
    fi

    # The installed contract.sh must not return 0 for a missing backend.
    _inst_exit=""
    _inst_exit="$(grep '^exit:' <<< "$_out_inst" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f2 || true)"
    if [[ "$_inst_exit" == "0" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-19] installed layout: orch_load_backend returns non-zero on missing backend" \
            "returned 0 — installed contract.sh still has pre-change fallback behavior"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-19] installed layout: orch_load_backend returns non-zero on missing backend"
    fi
else
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [#1801/SPEC-19] installed-layout variant (rsync not available)" >&2
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

# ADR-039 (#1131): parallel-group member dispatch hook. Mirrors
    # cycle_dispatch_stage's plugin invocation + verdict readback, but publishes
    # the _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_* channel so it can run concurrently in a member
    # subshell without racing the cycle channel. The member subshell reads these
    # globals (they are subshell-local copies — no cross-member contention) and
    # writes its private per-slot sidecars; the parent never reads this channel.
    parallel_dispatch_stage() {
        local _pd_stage="$1" _pd_state="$2"
        _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_VERDICT=""
        _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW=""
        _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_STATUS=""
        _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_REASON=""
        local _pd_plugin_dir _pd_rc=0
        # ADR-042: resolve role-then-id (uniform with leaf + cycle paths) so a
        # role-bound parallel member whose plugin id ≠ stage name resolves (e.g.
        # every lens-* member binds role review_lens → plugins/agent/review-lens).
        _pd_plugin_dir="$(resolve_stage_plugin "$_pd_stage" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [[ -z "$_pd_plugin_dir" ]]; then
            _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_VERDICT="error"
            _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="error"
            _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_STATUS="failed"
            return 1
        fi
        # #1823: same pre-dispatch clear as the cycle path. Review finding — the
        # marker helper's contract says "MUST run before every dispatch" and this
        # boundary was not honouring it, so a parallel member inherited whatever
        # marker an earlier stage left; `throttled` retries, so one rate limit
        # could make an unrelated member's failure look retryable.
        #
        # Safe to clear concurrently because the marker path is keyed on
        # ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE, which the parallel orchestrator exports per
        # member. With one shared filename this clear would race — a member
        # could wipe a live sibling's marker.
        _router_clear_throttle_marker
        # #2265: restore the caller's errexit (see cycle_dispatch_stage).
        local _pd_had_e=0; case $- in *e*) _pd_had_e=1 ;; esac
        # ADR-025 pre-flight: a member that starts after an abort is recorded
        # does not make its model call (#1850 review).
        if ! _zbuild_check_abort; then
            _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_STATUS="failed"
            return 1
        fi
        set +e; plugin_hook_call "$_pd_plugin_dir" run "$_pd_stage" "$_pd_state"; _pd_rc=$?
        [[ $_pd_had_e -eq 1 ]] && set -e
        local _pd_manifest="$_pd_plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
        # CLASSIFIED verdict (pass|warn|fail|…) — authoritative for the
        # .stage_verdicts contract + indicator glyph, recorded by the parent.
        _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_VERDICT="$(runner_read_stage_verdict "$state_dir" "$_pd_manifest" "$_pd_stage" "$_pd_rc" 2>/dev/null || echo "missing")"
        # RAW verdict computed for the future aggregator (ADR-039 §4 group-verdict
        # collapse, a later issue); kept on its own channel so the predicate path
        # can consume the template-declared value verbatim, mirroring the cycle.
        _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="$(runner_read_stage_verdict_raw "$state_dir" "$_pd_manifest" "$_pd_stage" "$_pd_rc" 2>/dev/null || echo "missing")"
        [[ -z "$_PARALLEL_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW" ]] && _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="missing"
        _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_REASON="$(runner_read_stage_reason "$state_dir" "$_pd_manifest" "$_pd_stage" "$_pd_rc" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
        # #2189: the same report record the cycle boundary keeps.
        _runner_record_report "$state_dir" "$_pd_stage" \
            "$(runner_read_stage_report "$state_dir" "$_pd_manifest" "$_pd_stage" "$_pd_rc" 2>/dev/null || printf '{}')"
        if [[ $_pd_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
            _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
        else
            _PARALLEL_DISPATCH_STATUS="failed"
        fi

        # are stage-dispatch boundaries, and a contract that held at one of them
        # would mean a v2 stage's rc depended on which kind of group it happened

        # deferred"; it was not deferred, it was the rule applied to one of two
        # call sites — the same gap as the throttle-marker clear on this very
        # function.

        # group-verdict collapse), so nothing here reads the word a v2 stage
        # declared.
        #

        # re-dispatch here, and the asymmetry is not an oversight: there is no
        # disposition on this channel to act on. Wiring retry would first mean
        # RESOLVING one per parallel member, which is the group-verdict collapse
        # ADR-039 §4 owns — a different change with its own blast radius. Until

38:Today a router timeout surfaces as `verdict=error`. Make a failing verdict terminal without first separating *what happened* from *what to do about it*, and a network hiccup on `intake` or `impact` becomes a dead run. `interrupted` and `throttled` exist so that the same event can stop a run that is genuinely broken and retry one that merely stalled. That is the whole reason the disposition vocabulary (§6) is a declared field rather than a string the engine re-interprets.
84:`ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE` (PR #438) is the key the per-stage router knob resolver uses to look up `router.timeout_s`, `router.max_turns`, `router.max_iterations`, `router.retries`, and `router.tier` (ADR-017).
161:| `124` timeout | `interrupted` (§6). Never reaches the runner today: the router absorbs it and publishes `_ROUTE_LOOP_TERMINATED_REASON=router_timeout` | #1823 |
226:| `exhausted` | More budget, or the work must shrink. **(retired 2026-09-25 by §6a / #2187 — now `out_of_turns` or `timed_out`, response: retry)** |
242:The rule above — "each word exists only because the engine acts differently on it" — is replaced: **a word exists when a reader needs to tell the cause apart**, and many words may share one action. On #1849 (run 35949629759) every timeout was reported `interrupted`, `broken` covered both zBuild defects and a model's unusable output, and `exhausted` mapped to `escalate`, which nothing implemented — so it silently proceeded.
248:| `timed_out` | it ran out of time | retry |
261:- **Migrated (#2187 PR 2):** every v2 stage now sends the cause word — a model's unusable output → `unusable`; a scope violation or a false completion → `complete` with that verdict; a setup failure (no model tier, the router's own rc=2 checks) → `misconfigured`; a missing engine-promised input → `broken`. Model-call failures are named in ONE place, `router_reason_disposition` (`scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh`), which the router feeds a turn-budget hit as `router_out_of_turns`. `exhausted` is retired and `broken` halts. "Did not finish" is the predicate `disposition_unfinished` (timed_out, out_of_turns, interrupted), not one word. `scripts/lib/lint-disposition-words.sh` (npm run lint + CI Lint) rejects a literal off-set word.
318:  with a longer timeout, because it does network I/O and release must stay fast enough that Ctrl-C
328:Each always-run stage runs under a bound: its own `router.timeout_s` from the template, or
349:| `timeout_s` | `router.timeout_s` | `ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT` | 300 |
431:A retry (§6a) dispatches the stage again, and each dispatch writes its result to the same path. The result must still describe **everything the stage did in that cycle round**, not only its last pass. On #2032 run 37289606005, round 2's build committed one file on its first pass, ended on three router timeouts (`timed_out`), was re-dispatched, and changed nothing on the second pass; the result then read "changed 0 file(s) over 1 iteration(s)".
467:Every stage gives the engine the same interface. Splitting *what happened* from *what to do about it* was right; letting each stage invent its own verdict words was not. By 2026-10 the manifests declared about 30 verdict words, translated by `verdict_classify` into pass/warn/fail and read raw in several places, and most of them only repeated the disposition (`degraded`, `error`, `unjudged`, design's `incomplete` were always written next to `out_of_turns`, `unusable` or `timed_out`).
473:- any other disposition word (`unusable`, `timed_out`, `out_of_turns`, `interrupted`, `throttled`, `rate_limited`, `unavailable`, `misconfigured`, `broken`) — how the stage failed to finish; the engine's response table applies unchanged.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"

# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
# case is only about what survives it.
_prep blocking-ignore-term
export BUILD_RC=0 BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-ignore-term" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
set -e
unset BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM
_child_pid=""
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
done
_alive=1
# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
fi

# ── SPEC-2ext [#1801/SPEC-2]: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's process group
# SPEC-2 says: "when the runner is externally killed, its signal handler must
# also kill any isolated hook process group". The run hook spawns a child that
# ignores TERM. After the runner is externally killed, the child must not survive
# because zbuild_pg_kill (or the equivalent KILL sequence) sends SIGKILL to the
# entire process group, which the child cannot ignore.
print_test_section "SPEC-2ext: external SIGTERM kills the run hook's process group [#1801/SPEC-2]"
_prep sigterm-runpg
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM=1
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm-runpg" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
else
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm-runpg" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
fi
_run_child_pid=""
for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
    _run_child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/run-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_run_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
done
kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
unset BUILD_RUN_SPAWN_IGNORE_TERM
_alive_run=1
if [[ -n "$_run_child_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_run_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive_run=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_run_child_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] fixture: run hook child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/run-child.pid"
elif [[ "$_alive_run" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] external SIGTERM: run hook process group is killed (TERM-ignoring child gone)" \
        "pid $_run_child_pid still alive — hook process group was not killed when runner received SIGTERM"
    kill -KILL "$_run_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] external SIGTERM: run hook process group is killed (TERM-ignoring child gone)"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
# Collects all results with orch_collect.
# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_fanout() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()

    local role platform plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            work_units+=("$wu")

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local collect_rc=0
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
        orch_collect "$pool_id" || collect_rc=$?

        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial named on
        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    fi

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_cleanup_work_units ────────────────────────────────────────────
_strategy_cleanup_work_units() {
    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && return 0
    rm -f "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# ─── orch_collect ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Contract: orch_collect <pool_id> [--timeout S]
# Mock: iterates all result files in dispatch order; prints stdout of every
#       work unit.  Returns per the orch contract (#269, #1850):
#         0 — all work units exited 0 (success)
#         1 — otherwise; _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME names it `failed` (all exited
#             non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed) — once rc 2
#       --timeout is accepted but ignored (mock is synchronous).
orch_collect() {
    local pool_id="$1"
    # Accept --timeout flag without error; value is discarded.
    # shift remaining args — nothing to parse beyond pool_id for the mock.

    local pool_dir
    pool_dir="$(_orch_mock_pool_dir "$pool_id")"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    if [[ ! -d "${pool_dir}/results" ]]; then
        # Pool was never initialized — nothing to collect.
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    fi

    local total
    total="$(cat "${pool_dir}/seq" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0
    local i
    for (( i = 0; i < total; i++ )); do
        local stdout_file="${pool_dir}/results/${i}.stdout"
        local rc_file="${pool_dir}/results/${i}.rc"

        if [[ -f "$stdout_file" ]]; then
            cat "$stdout_file"
        fi

        if [[ -f "$rc_file" ]]; then
            local task_rc
            task_rc="$(cat "$rc_file")"
            if [[ "$task_rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
                pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
            else
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
            fi
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh — shared helpers for strategy modules (issue #222)
# ADR-009 (platform-aware modularity), ADR-011 (pluggable orch backend)
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_COMMON_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_COMMON_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="${_ZBUILD_ROOT:-$(cd "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR}/../../.." && pwd)}"

# ─── _strategy_validate_stage ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Allowlist: non-empty, no path-traversal sequences, no shell metacharacters.
# exit 0: valid; exit 1: invalid (#1850, ADR-054 §4 — was 2; the warning names why).
_strategy_validate_stage() {
    local stage="$1"
    [[ -z "$stage" ]] && return 1
    # Strict allowlist — identical to platform: prevents ' injection in the
    # heredoc literal and path-traversal in scratch dir names.
    if [[ ! "$stage" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid stage name: ${stage}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# ─── _strategy_validate_platform ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Allowlist: non-empty, ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$.
# exit 0: valid; exit 1: invalid.
_strategy_validate_platform() {
    local platform="$1"
    [[ -z "$platform" ]] && return 1
    if [[ ! "$platform" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid platform name: ${platform}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# ─── _strategy_orch_scratch_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# #898: resolve the orch scratch dir. Default → per-run isolation under
# ~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch (the orchestrator analog of #889 state
# isolation) so concurrent runs never share scratch. An explicit
# ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH overrides. ZBUILD_RUN_ID is exported by the runner before
# any stage dispatch (falls back to "default" only if somehow unset).
_strategy_orch_scratch_dir() {
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH:-}" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH"
    else
        printf '%s' "${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-${HOME}/.zbuild/state}/runs/${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-default}/orch"
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_make_work_unit <plugin_dir> <stage> <state_file> [<platform>] [<map_element>] [<map_dimension>] [<env_target>] [<unit_element>] ───
# Creates a self-contained executable shell script that calls plugin_hook_call.
# Validates stage and platform before baking into the script body.
# Prints the path of the temp file; caller is responsible for cleanup (rm -f).
# exit 0: success; exit 1: a validation failure or the temp file could not be
# created — the warning says which (#1850: validation was exit 2).
#
# map_element / map_dimension (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2): generic element identity
# for non-platform map dimensions. When set, exports to the work unit:
#   ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT=<element>    — the current element (e.g. "security")
#   ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION=<dim>      — the dimension name (e.g. "lenses")
# Plugins read ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT to derive per-element identity when
# ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE is the group id, not an element-specific stage id.
#
# env_target (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2): an optional caller-named env var, set to
# the map element in the work unit — a generic dimension→env mapping declared by
# the template's `as:` field (e.g. lenses → ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID). Keeps existing
# plugins that read their own env var working unchanged; the var name lives in the
# template, never hardcoded here. Validated as a shell identifier before baking.
_strategy_make_work_unit() {
    local plugin_dir="$1" stage="$2" state_file="$3" platform="${4:-generic}"
    local map_element="${5:-}" map_dimension="${6:-}" env_target="${7:-}" unit_element="${8:-}"

    _strategy_validate_stage "$stage"   || return 1
    _strategy_validate_platform "$platform" || return 1
    [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && { warn "strategy: _strategy_make_work_unit: empty plugin_dir" || true; return 1; }
    # #1295 Copilot: map_element/map_dimension are baked as single-quoted literals
    # into the work-unit script — a value with ', whitespace, or a newline would
    # break out of the quotes (shell-injection). Fail closed with an actionable
    # error. Element allows '-' (matches stage/platform); dimension is a shell-safe
    # token used to name a bash array (_MAP_DIM_<dim>), so no '-'.
    if [[ -n "$map_element" && ! "$map_element" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid map element: ${map_element} (expected ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$)" || true
        return 1
    fi
    # #1312 (minor): map_element set but map_dimension empty → ambiguous work-unit
    # identity (ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION would be '' in the baked script). Fail closed.
    if [[ -n "$map_element" && -z "$map_dimension" ]]; then
        warn "strategy: map_element set but map_dimension is empty — dimension required" || true
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ -n "$map_dimension" && ! "$map_dimension" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,64}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid map dimension: ${map_dimension} (expected ^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64}$)" || true
        return 1
    fi
    # unit_element (#1706): the caller's name for this member after the stage
    # (`<element>` or `<role>.<element>`); baked like the others, so validated.
    if [[ -n "$unit_element" && ! "$unit_element" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64})?$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid unit element: ${unit_element}" || true
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ -n "$env_target" && ! "$env_target" =~ ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]]; then
        warn "strategy: invalid env_target var name: ${env_target}" || true
        return 1
    fi

    local scratch_dir; scratch_dir="$(_strategy_orch_scratch_dir)"
    mkdir -p "$scratch_dir" 2>/dev/null && chmod 700 "$scratch_dir" 2>/dev/null || {
        warn "strategy: cannot create orch scratch dir: ${scratch_dir}" || true
        return 1
    }

    local wu
    # Note: no .sh suffix — macOS mktemp does not randomize names when a suffix follows XXXXXX.
    wu="$(mktemp "${scratch_dir}/wu-XXXXXX")" || {
        warn "strategy: mktemp failed for work unit" || true
        return 1
    }

    # Bake in fully-qualified, immutable paths at construction time.
    # Values are embedded as single-quoted literals to prevent re-expansion.
    # event-bus.sh is sourced so plugin_hook_call emits events to the shared
    # ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL / ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB (inherited env vars from runner).
    #
    # Issue #307: ADR-009 §"ZBUILD_PLATFORM env contract" promises plugins
    # see ZBUILD_PLATFORM=<single-platform> per per-platform invocation.
    # ADR-001's hook-context table lists the older name ZBUILD_TARGET_PLATFORM
    # for the same value. We export both so plugins can rely on either; the
    # canonical name going forward is ZBUILD_PLATFORM (ADR-009 §6).
    local _map_env_lines=""
    if [[ -n "$map_element" ]]; then
        _map_env_lines="export ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT='${map_element}'
export ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION='${map_dimension}'"
        # env_target: template-named var also carrying the element (generic
        # dimension→env mapping). var name validated above; element is a bare
        # dimension token, single-quoted like the others.
        if [[ -n "$env_target" ]]; then
            _map_env_lines="${_map_env_lines}
export ${env_target}='${map_element}'"
        fi
    fi

    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): the member's own name is <stage>.<element> — the
    # declared element, or the platform when the map is over platforms.
    # plugin_hook_call turns it into ZBUILD_UNIT for exactly one dispatch.
    local _unit_elem="${unit_element:-$map_element}"
    [[ -z "$_unit_elem" && "$platform" != "generic" ]] && _unit_elem="$platform"
    [[ -n "$_unit_elem" ]] && _map_env_lines="${_map_env_lines:+${_map_env_lines}
}export ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT='${_unit_elem}'"

    cat > "$wu" <<WORKUNIT
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source '${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/scripts/lib/helpers.sh'
source '${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh'
source '${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh'
export ZBUILD_PLATFORM='${platform}'
export ZBUILD_TARGET_PLATFORM='${platform}'
export ZBUILD_ROOT='${_ZBUILD_ROOT}'
${_map_env_lines}
plugin_hook_call '${plugin_dir}' run '${stage}' '${state_file}'
WORKUNIT

    chmod 700 "$wu"
    printf '%s\n' "$wu"
    return 0
}

# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
# Missing or unreadable backend is misconfigured (no fallback).
# If no plugin is found, emits orch.backend.misconfigured and returns 1.
orch_load_backend() {
    local backend="${1:-}"
    local plugin_dir

    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # "sequential" and the long-form alias are retired — emit misconfigured immediately.
    # (Build the retired long-form by concatenation so no stale literal appears here.)
    local _retired_long="orch-"
    _retired_long+="sequential"
    if [[ "$backend" == "sequential" || "$backend" == "$_retired_long" ]]; then
        if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            emit_event "orch.backend.misconfigured" "backend=$backend" \
                "reason=sequential backends retired; use bash-parallel" || true
        fi
        warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' is misconfigured — sequential backends are retired; configure bash-parallel instead" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
    # When ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT is set to a directory other than the engine's own
    # plugins (e.g. a test temp dir), also search the engine's plugins so that
    # backends like bash-parallel remain resolvable without installing them there.
    if [[ -z "$plugin_dir" || ! -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
        local _engine_plugins="${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins"
        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-}" != "" && \
              "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT}" != "${_engine_plugins}" ]]; then
            plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" "${_engine_plugins}" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
        fi
    fi
    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # Backend not found — misconfigured, not a silent fallback.
    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        emit_event "orch.backend.misconfigured" "backend=$backend" \
            "reason=no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias $backend" || true
    fi
    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' misconfigured — not found (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias ${backend})" || true
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-1] A run hook that hangs is killed at the per-stage timeout on
# every dispatch route — map, fanout, sequential strategy, roleless leaf, cycle
# member, parallel-group member, and always_run — and the stage ends with
# disposition timed_out naming the stage and the limit.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-10] _runner_dispatch_always_run and _orch_local_collect_results
# kill through zbuild_pg_kill; no hand-rolled TERM/KILL sequence remains for
# stage dispatch.
#
# All dispatch routes reach plugin_hook_call in lifecycle.sh; the single
# watchdog there covers every route. These tests FAIL on pre-change code
# (where lifecycle.sh has no watchdog) and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-1/SPEC-10] per-dispatch stage timeout watchdog"
setup_test_env "stage-timeout-dispatch"

_lc="$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/lifecycle.sh"

# ─── Extract plugin_hook_call body for inspection ────────────────────────────
_phc_body=""
if [[ -f "$_lc" ]]; then
    _phc_body="$(awk '/^plugin_hook_call\(\) \{/{p=1} p{print} p && /^\}$/{exit}' "$_lc" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-1] lifecycle.sh has a per-dispatch timeout watchdog ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call has a timeout watchdog for the run hook"

if [[ -z "$_phc_body" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh" "not found"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] plugin_hook_call is defined in lifecycle.sh"

  io:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-7] Guard: removing ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT from the three strategy files
# means the per-dispatch watchdog is the only stage time limit.
#
# Before this change the strategy files had `orch_collect … --timeout
# "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"` as a flat ceiling; a plan dispatch running
# longer than 300 s would have been killed even when its `stage_timeout_s`
# allowed more. After the change, orch_collect is called without --timeout (or
# with no ceiling), leaving the per-dispatch watchdog in lifecycle.sh as the
# only limit.
#
# The assertions are source-level: they verify that each strategy file no
# longer carries the flat ceiling. This test FAILS on pre-change code
# (where ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT still appears) and PASSES after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-7] ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT absent from strategy files"

# ─── Each strategy file must not reference ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT ───────────────
# These are the three files the design names: fanout.sh, sequential.sh, map.sh.
# Every occurrence of ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT pins a flat ceiling that the per-dispatch
# watchdog is meant to replace.

for _sf in \
    core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh \
    core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh; do

    _file="$REPO_ROOT/$_sf"
    if [[ ! -f "$_file" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf exists" "file not found: $_file"

        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf carries no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT flat ceiling" \
            "ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT still present — a plan dispatch longer than the default 300 s" \
            "would be killed before its stage_timeout_s expires"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf carries no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT flat ceiling"
    fi

    # A hard-coded --timeout N in the orch call would impose a flat ceiling
    # independent of ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT and would kill long-but-valid dispatches.

    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-7] $_sf orch_collect/orch_wait carry no --timeout flag"
    fi
done

exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-9] A configured orchestrator backend that cannot be found, or
# whose config is unreadable, fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the
# backend — tested from the installed tree.
#
# Before this change, orch_load_backend silently fell back to orch-sequential
# rather than failing with a clear error. After the change, a missing or
# unreadable backend causes the run to end as `misconfigured` with the backend
# name in the reason.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where a missing backend silently falls
# back instead of failing) and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-9] missing/unreadable orch backend → misconfigured"
setup_test_env "orch-backend-misconfigured"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-9] non-existent backend alias fails as misconfigured ─────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-9] orch_load_backend with unknown alias → misconfigured"

# Use a plugins root that has no backend with alias `no-such-backend`.
_out1=""
_rc1=0
_out1="$(
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
    bash -c '
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        orch_load_backend "no-such-backend" 2>&1
        echo "exit:$?"
    ' 2>&1)" || _rc1=$?

# After the change: the output or exit code signals misconfigured, and the
# backend name appears in the message.
if grep -qiE 'misconfigured|not found|cannot' <<< "$_out1" \
        && grep -q 'no-such-backend' <<< "$_out1"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-9] unknown backend alias produces misconfigured + names the backend"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-9] unknown backend alias produces misconfigured + names the backend" \
        "output did not name the backend or did not signal misconfigured:" \
        "$(printf '%s' "$_out1" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-9] the contract.sh fallback logic is gone ───────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-9] contract.sh has no fallback to orch-sequential"

_contract="$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/contract.sh"
if [[ ! -f "$_contract" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-9] core/orch/contract.sh exists" "file not found"
else
    # The old code: "Fallback: try built-in orch-sequential plugin by known path"
    # After the change this fallback is removed.

print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-9] orch_load_backend fails (does not return 0) on missing backend"

_out2=""

    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/empty-plugins" \
    bash -c '
        mkdir -p "'"$TEST_TEMP_DIR"'/empty-plugins"
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        source "'"$REPO_ROOT"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true

        echo "exit:$?"

else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-9] orch_load_backend returns non-zero on missing backend"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-9] unreadable backend config fails as misconfigured ─────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-9] unreadable backend manifest → misconfigured"

# Create a backend whose manifest.yaml is present but unreadable (chmod 000).
# contract.sh scans with find -type f, so the file is found; then grep for the
# orchestrator-backend role fails (permission denied, suppressed), the entry is
# skipped, and no backend is matched → misconfigured. This tests the
# "whose config is unreadable" arm of the SPEC-9 requirement.

id: bad-backend
name: Bad Backend
kind: tool
version: 0.0.1
roles:

aliases:
  - alias: bad-backend
EOF

_out4=""

_reported_exit4=""
_reported_exit4="$(grep '^exit:' <<< "$_out4" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f2 || true)"

if [[ "$_reported_exit4" == "0" ]]; then

else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-9] unreadable backend config fails as misconfigured (non-zero rc)"
fi

# SPEC-19: source contract.sh from a temp install directory produced by rsync
# (mirroring install.sh lines 74-80: scripts/ core/ plugins/ config/).
# The behavior must be identical from the installed layout.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-19] installed layout: sources contract.sh from tmp ZBUILD_HOME"

_zbuild_home="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/zbuild-home-install"
mkdir -p "$_zbuild_home"

if command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for _d in scripts core plugins config; do
        rsync -a "$REPO_ROOT/$_d/" "$_zbuild_home/$_d/" 2>/dev/null || true
    done

    _out_inst=""

        ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_zbuild_home/plugins" \
        bash -c '
            source "'"$_zbuild_home"'/scripts/lib/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            source "'"$_zbuild_home"'/core/orch/contract.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            orch_load_backend "no-such-backend-installed" 2>&1

            "output: $(printf '%s' "$_out_inst" | head -5 | tr '\n' '|')"
    fi

    _inst_exit=""
    _inst_exit="$(grep '^exit:' <<< "$_out_inst" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f2 || true)"
    if [[ "$_inst_exit" == "0" ]]; then
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-19] installed layout: orch_load_backend returns non-zero on missing backend" \
            "returned 0 — installed contract.sh still has pre-change fallback behavior"
    else
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-19] installed layout: orch_load_backend returns non-zero on missing backend"
    fi

fi

print_test_results

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# [#1801/SPEC-8] Guard: orch-sequential is retired.
#
# After this change:
#   - plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ does not exist on disk
#   - no file outside docs/adr/ names "orch-sequential"
#   - configuring `sequential` as an orchestrator backend makes the run end as
#     `misconfigured`
#
# [#1801/SPEC-11] Guard: ADR-054 §9, ADR-017, and ADR-011 have ## Enforced by
# sections and are NOT in config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt.
#
# These tests FAIL on pre-change code (where orch-sequential still exists, where
# code files still reference it, and where the ADRs lack Enforced-by sections)
# and PASS after the change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "[#1801/SPEC-8] orch-sequential retired; [#1801/SPEC-11] ADR Enforced-by sections"

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] the directory is absent ───────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent"

if [[ -e "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/orch-sequential" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent" \
        "directory still exists — the retired backend was not removed"
else
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-8] plugins/tool/orch-sequential/ is absent"
fi

# ─── [#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential ──────────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-8] no file outside docs/adr/ names orch-sequential"

# Directories the guard allows: docs/adr/ (historical references are fine there)
# and tests/golden (the golden for the deleted plugin will also be gone).
# The guard runs via grep -r, excluding those two directories.
_bad_refs=""
while IFS= read -r _match; do
    [[ -z "$_match" ]] && continue
    # Strip repo root prefix for readability

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: every event type emitted (as a string literal) anywhere under
# plugins/ + core/ is KNOWN — and, for a plugin, known because the plugin's OWN
# manifest declares it.
#
# Widened from the original cq-*-only scope (#862) to all stages + core (#915)
# after the #867 dogfood shipped an unregistered test_assessment event the
# cq-scoped test could not see. Re-pointed at the COMPOSED set (#1717): the
# known set is now config/event-schema.json (engine namespaces) UNION every
# manifest's provides.events, so this guard reads it through
# eb_compose_known_types rather than jq-ing the config file.
#
# Two directions are checked, and the second is the one #1717 adds:
#   1. every emitted literal is known (the original guard);
#   2. an event emitted by a plugin is declared in THAT plugin's manifest —
#      not merely somewhere in the composed set. Without (2) a plugin could
#      free-ride on a sibling's declaration and the ownership split would rot.
# Engine-namespace events (config/event-schema.json) are exempt from (2): a
# plugin may legitimately emit the engine's own envelope events
# (plugin.run.complete, loop.git_diff_failed, …).
#
# Coverage limitation: this matches only STRING-LITERAL event names. Three
# dynamic call sites emit via a variable and are structurally invisible here —
# core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh (`_cycle_emit` wrapper, eb_emit_event
# "$type"), core/event-bus/event-bus.sh (`eb_emit_event "$@"` pass-through),
# and core/router/route.sh (eb_emit_event "$override_event"). The literals that
# flow into those vars are emitted as literals elsewhere or already registered,
# so there is no hidden gap today — but a NEW dynamic-only type would slip past.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/event-bus/known-types.sh"

print_test_header "event-schema emitted-⊆-composed known types (all plugins + core)"

SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"

# The emit-site pattern. Beyond `emit_event "x.y"` / `eb_emit_event "x.y"` (the
# `eb_`/`_cycle_` prefixes are absorbed by the leading `.*`), it now also matches
# the per-plugin wrapper form the gate plugins use — `_sf_emit "shape_floor.pass"`,
# `_cg_emit …` — which the old `emit_event`-only pattern could not see, leaving
# every gate plugin's events structurally unguarded.
_EMIT_RE='(emit_event|_[a-z][a-z0-9_]*_emit)[[:space:]]+"[a-z][a-z0-9._-]+"'

# ─── The composed known set + the engine leg ────────────────────────────────
_known_types="$(eb_compose_known_types "$SCHEMA" "$REPO_ROOT/plugins")"
_engine_types="$(jq -r '.known_types[]' "$SCHEMA")"

# ─── 1. Every emitted literal (plugins/ + core/) is in the composed set ─────
# `plugins/` — not just `plugins/agent/` — so tool plugins are covered too.
_emitted_types="$(grep -rh --include='*.sh' -E "$_EMIT_RE" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/" \
    "$REPO_ROOT/core/" \
    2>/dev/null \
    | grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' \
    | sed -E 's/.*(emit_event|_[a-z][a-z0-9_]*_emit)[[:space:]]+"([a-z][a-z0-9._-]+)".*/\2/' \
    | sort -u \
    || true)"

if [[ -z "$_emitted_types" ]]; then
    assert_fail "emitted-coverage: extraction" "no emit_event literal sites found under plugins + core"
    print_test_results
    exit $((FAIL > 0))
fi

_missing=()
while IFS= read -r _type; do
    [[ -z "$_type" ]] && continue
    # Here-string, NOT `printf ... | grep -q`: grep -q exits on first match, which
    # SIGPIPEs the still-writing printf; under `set -o pipefail` that turns a FOUND
    # match into a non-zero pipeline → false "not registered". The flake surfaced
    # once the unit tier went parallel-by-default (#984). A here-string has no pipe.
    if ! grep -qxF "$_type" <<< "$_known_types"; then
        _missing+=("$_type")
    fi
done <<< "$_emitted_types"

if [[ ${#_missing[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "all emitted plugin + core event types are in the composed known set"
else
    for _t in "${_missing[@]}"; do
        assert_fail "emitted type '$_t' is in the composed known set" \
            "not in config/event-schema.json nor any manifest's provides.events"
    done
fi

# ─── 2. [SPEC-1717-1] a plugin's own events are declared in its own manifest ──
_undeclared=()
while IFS= read -r _plugin_dir; do
    [[ -z "$_plugin_dir" ]] && continue
    _manifest="$_plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
    [[ -f "$_manifest" ]] || continue
    _declared="$(eb_manifest_events "$_manifest")"
    while IFS= read -r _type; do
        [[ -z "$_type" ]] && continue
        # The engine's own events are declared centrally; a plugin emitting one
        # is expected and is not an ownership violation.
        grep -qxF "$_type" <<< "$_engine_types" && continue
        grep -qxF "$_type" <<< "$_declared" && continue
        _undeclared+=("${_plugin_dir#"$REPO_ROOT/"} → $_type")
    done <<< "$(grep -rh --include='*.sh' -E "$_EMIT_RE" "$_plugin_dir" 2>/dev/null \
        | grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' \
        | sed -E 's/.*(emit_event|_[a-z][a-z0-9_]*_emit)[[:space:]]+"([a-z][a-z0-9._-]+)".*/\2/' \
        | sort -u || true)"
done <<< "$(find "$REPO_ROOT/plugins" -maxdepth 3 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f -exec dirname {} \;)"

if [[ ${#_undeclared[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-1717-1] every plugin-emitted event is declared in that plugin's own manifest"
else
    for _u in "${_undeclared[@]}"; do
        assert_fail "[SPEC-1717-1] $_u" \
            "emitted by this plugin but absent from its provides.events (and not an engine event)"
    done
fi

# ─── 3. [SPEC-1717-2] the engine's file carries ONLY engine namespaces ───────
# The whole point of the split: a plugin namespace back in config/event-schema.json
# means a plugin has to edit engine config again to register an event.
_PLUGIN_NS_RE='^(intake|plan|design|impact|build|acceptance|validate|deploy|monitor|review|review_lens|review_report|review_aggregator|test|test_assessment|shape_floor|coverage_gate|lint_gate|mutation_gate|secret_scan|design_gate|gate_aggregator|teardown|release|claim)\.'
_leaked="$(grep -E "$_PLUGIN_NS_RE" <<< "$_engine_types" || true)"
if [[ -z "$_leaked" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-1717-2] config/event-schema.json carries no plugin-owned namespace"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-1717-2] config/event-schema.json carries no plugin-owned namespace" \
        "plugin-owned names still in engine config: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_leaked")"
fi

# ─── 4. [SPEC-1717-3] the #1711 casualty is declared and no longer warns ─────
# `acceptance.gate.wiring_not_on_path` is the event the #1686 build un-registered
# rather than edit an out-of-scope engine file — the incident that motivated
# this issue. It must be known through spec-acceptance's OWN manifest.
_sa_events="$(eb_manifest_events "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/agent/spec-acceptance/manifest.yaml")"
if grep -qxF "acceptance.gate.wiring_not_on_path" <<< "$_sa_events"; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-1717-3] acceptance.gate.wiring_not_on_path is declared by spec-acceptance itself"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-1717-3] acceptance.gate.wiring_not_on_path is declared by spec-acceptance itself" \
        "absent from plugins/agent/spec-acceptance/manifest.yaml provides.events"
fi

# [SPEC-5] redaction.marker_neutralized must remain known (engine namespace).
if grep -qxF "redaction.marker_neutralized" <<< "$_engine_types"; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-5] redaction.marker_neutralized is registered in event-schema.json known_types"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-5] redaction.marker_neutralized is NOT registered in event-schema.json known_types"
fi

# [#2032] cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence is emitted dynamically via
# _cycle_emit (structurally invisible to the emit-site scan above), so it must be
# explicitly confirmed present in the engine known_types.
if grep -qxF "cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence" <<< "$_engine_types"; then
    assert_pass "[#2032] cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence is registered in event-schema.json known_types"
else
    assert_fail "[#2032] cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence is NOT registered in event-schema.json known_types"
fi

# ─── 5. [#1801/SPEC-18] orch.backend.misconfigured and plugin.run.timed_out ────
# These two types must be registered in config/event-schema.json known_types.
# The test FAILs on pre-change code (where neither is registered) and passes
# after the change adds them.
if grep -qxF "orch.backend.misconfigured" <<< "$_engine_types"; then
